processing: Typical of Kenyan black tea, much of it is machine-processed by the CTC (crush, tear, curl) method for a fast, strong brew, though some orthodox tea is also sold under the Kericho name.
harvest_season: Kenyan highland tea is generally picked through most of the year, without the sharp seasons of northern tea regions.
appearance_dry: Typical of CTC tea, small dark granules with a brownish cast.
appearance_liquor: Typically a bright, deep reddish copper.
taste_profile: As with other Kenyan CTC teas, brisk and bright with solid malt, and strong enough to take milk.

brewing.notes: A usual Western-style steep for CTC tea; it brews quickly and turns harsh if left long. Good with milk.

vintage_note: Usual for Kenyan CTC tea, it is sold by grade and mostly goes into blends and tea bags, without vintages. Single-estate packs are less common; buy fresh and check the packing date.
description:
Kericho tea comes from the highlands around Kericho in western Kenya, an area commonly linked with Kenyan tea. It is a place name and not a tightly defined style.

As with other Kenyan black teas, much of it is made by CTC, which turns leaf into small granules that give up colour and strength quickly.

Expect a brisk, bright cup. Keep the steep short, and use milk freely if you like, since this kind of tea is built for it.

Most of it disappears anonymously into blends, so a pack naming Kericho and its estate or factory is the one to look for.
history: Little is documented here about how tea in Kericho developed, so no dates or founders are given. Today the area is known for large tea estates alongside smaller growers.
